lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 19: Ingress and Gateway API basics
lesson.description: Route HTTP into a kind cluster by host, path and header: an Ingress with its controller, then the same routes as a Gateway API HTTPRoute.
lesson.tested: Ingress and HTTPRoute via Traefik v3.7.17, Gateway API v1.6.3, kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.cluster: kind lab, Traefik in namespace traefik
lesson.rule: An Ingress or HTTPRoute is only a rule; a controller makes it real. New work should start on Gateway API, where the Gateway owner decides which namespaces may attach routes.

rows.name: Ingress or HTTPRoute
rows.role: A stored rule. A controller Pod watches the rules and configures a proxy; without it nothing happens.

rows.name: Ingress NGINX
rows.role: The Ingress API is frozen and Ingress NGINX was retired on 24 March 2026. Check your clusters with the ingress-nginx selector, and start new routing on Gateway API.

rows.name: Gateway API roles
rows.role: GatewayClass for the controller, Gateway for listeners and allowedRoutes, HTTPRoute for the app's matches and backends.

rows.name: Route status
rows.role: Accepted=False means the Gateway refused the route. ResolvedRefs=False means a backend is wrong. The most specific match wins, and a longer path prefix beats a header match.

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from earlier parts and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lab used Traefik v3.7.17 and Gateway API v1.6.3. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: Why is an Ingress or HTTPRoute not enough on its own?
exercises.a: It is only a stored rule. A controller Pod must be running to watch the rules and configure a proxy. Without that controller, nothing happens. The CLASS column must name an IngressClass whose controller is running.

exercises.q: What happened to Ingress NGINX, and what should you start new work on?
exercises.a: Ingress NGINX was retired on 24 March 2026. Since then it gets no releases, bug fixes or security updates, and its GitHub repository is archived. Check clusters with kubectl get pods -A --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx, and start new routing on Gateway API.

exercises.q: What do GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute each own?
exercises.a: GatewayClass names the controller. Gateway holds listeners and allowedRoutes, so the Gateway owner decides which namespaces may attach routes. HTTPRoute holds the app's host, path and header matches and its backends.

exercises.q: You create an Ingress for legacy.example.test with ingressClassName: nginx, but Traefik is the only controller. What does a request return, and what fixes it?
exercises.a: Traefik ignores that Ingress and returns 404. After you patch ingressClassName to traefik, the same request returns the backend response within a few seconds.

exercises.q: How does the lab send traffic to the in-cluster proxy?
exercises.a: kubectl port-forward to the Traefik Service on 8080:80, then curl with a Host header of shop.example.test so the proxy can match the route.

exercises.q: After you switch the same routes to Gateway API, what status field shows that a listener accepted the HTTPRoute?
exercises.a: kubectl get gateway ... -o jsonpath on status.listeners shows attachedRoutes. Route status Accepted=False would mean the Gateway refused the route; ResolvedRefs=False would mean a backend is wrong.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: Two HTTPRoute rules could match a request: a short path prefix and a longer path prefix plus a header. Which wins?
exercises.a: The most specific match wins, and a longer path prefix beats a header match, as the lesson states.

exercises.q: A Gateway's allowedRoutes does not include the HTTPRoute's namespace. What status do you expect?
exercises.a: Accepted=False: the Gateway refused the route. The Gateway owner decides which namespaces may attach routes.
